boundary_note: Bounded first pass for all five frozen records in the Confederate Heartland Offensive. Preserve per-engagement dates; the live NPS campaign heading (June-October 1862) does not replace any battle interval. Opening personnel and exact effective command boundaries remain unresolved. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. Imported numerical estimates remain unchanged; this pass does not validate them as simultaneous opening forces.

claims.value: The frozen force field names formations without counts; the live NPS field reads zero. Cist gives Nelson's entire command as some 7,000 and the Confederate force as 12,000 with 36 guns.
claims.rationale: Cist's figures are retrospective estimates of whole commands, not matched engaged populations at an opening boundary. NPS says troops joined both sides during the day. Live zeros are not measured absence.

claims.value: NPS places Manson's August 30 battle line near Zion Church. Cist describes a line about two miles from Richmond on the 29th and, on the 30th, a line beyond Rogersville, a new line a mile to the rear that was badly posted, the previous day's line, and a last stand at the camps.
claims.rationale: Sequential positions, not map-verified terrain. 'Badly posted' is Cist's retrospective judgment.

claims.value: NPS says Manson commanded Union forces in the area and Cleburne led the Confederate advance until Smith and Nelson arrived and took command; Cist likewise says Nelson assumed command on arriving.
claims.rationale: The frozen principal commanders arrived during the engagement. Field and army command are distinct; neither receives automatic sole credit, and no exact transfer clock is established. The live heading ranks Smith as Lieutenant General, against the frozen Major General; the heading is not adopted.

open_questions: Original returns, casualty reconciliation, contemporary message chains, the August 29 skirmish population and precise command-transfer clocks remain deferred after the bounded pass. No map verification is claimed.
NPS/CWSAC is one family; Cist is one interested retrospective Union staff history. Quoted reports and participant accounts inside Cist are not additional independently inspected families.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
